top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks with Katori and Ye is a mature, independently reproduced result (magic-wavelength lattice, 10^-18 performance confirmed at RIKEN/Tokyo, JILA, NIST, PTB, SYRTE, NPL) that also queries nature through millimetre-scale redshift and bounds on varying constants and dark-matter couplings, even if these are so far null. The two-name allocation is clean, the citation isolates the lattice concept from the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes, and the remaining priority question is for the expert reports. Aberration-corrected TEM is a real, verified invention but is an enabling instrument with an unresolved STEM-corrector attribution, so I rank it second ahead of no award.
